name: Video Depth Anything
plain: Video Depth Anything (ByteDance): depth of a whole video, consistent from frame to frame, in windows of 32 frames on the Depth Anything V2 Small encoder; relative and metric. Apache-2.0 code and weights (Small only).
summary: Video Depth Anything (Chen et al., CVPR 2025): temporally consistent depth of long videos from the Depth Anything V2 encoder and a DPT head with temporal attention, run in overlapping 32-frame windows; relative (Small) and metric (Metric Small) checkpoints.

papers.title: Video Depth Anything: Consistent Depth Estimation for Super-Long Videos

licence_notes: Only the Small checkpoints (relative and metric) are Apache-2.0; the Base and Large checkpoints are CC-BY-NC-4.0 and not included.
The metric model is trained on Virtual KITTI 2 (CC BY-NC-SA 3.0) and IRS per the upstream README (a note only).
limitations: A call's batch is one video in time order: frames are not independent (each window attends over time and is aligned to the previous one), so a batch is not the same as single calls.
Every call runs at least one 32-frame window (shorter videos are padded with copies of their last frame): one image costs about as much as 32 frames in the temporal head.
The whole video's depth is kept on the device as float32 (L x H x W); split very long videos.
task_io: Input: one RGB image. Output: a depth or inverse-depth map. `kind` (a card field, `result.kind`) says what the numbers mean: `metric` = metres; `scale_invariant`, `affine_invariant` and `affine_invariant_inverse` are relative (unknown scale or shift, not metres). Metric models that use the focal length take `model(image, intrinsics=K)` (K `[3, 3]`, pixels of the input): `metric3d-vit-large` and `da3metric-large` need it for correct metres (`da3metric-large`: metres = output x focal / 300; without `intrinsics=` a 300 px focal length is assumed, wrong for a real camera). `unidepth-v2-vitl14`, `unik3d-vitl`, `depth-pro` and MoGe estimate the camera themselves (given `intrinsics=` replace `fx`); `zoedepth-nk` and the relative models (`da3mono-large` too) take none. Normals-only models (`kind` `none`) return `result.normals` `[B, H, W, 3]` (unit vectors, camera frame: x right, y down, z forward).
